$comment: Machine-readable enforcement policy — Agent OS v1, 2026-08-04.
Matching layer rebuilt 2026-08-04 after an adversarial review proved 22 end-to-end bypasses
and 7 false positives in the first draft. Every verified bypass string below is now a
denyExample and every verified false positive an allowExample — the canary locks both.
Consumers:  scripts/agent-os/pretool.mjs (the hook) · scripts/agent-os/policy.test.mjs (canaries).
Macros:     __GIT__<verb> expands (in policy.mjs) to a git stem that tolerates global options
(git -C <path> push, git -c k=v push, --git-dir=…), which otherwise defeat every rule.
Preprocess: quoted -m/--message/--title/--body arguments are replaced with <ARG> before matching
(mention ≠ execution), and a single unchained read-only command (rg/grep/git log…)
skips command rules entirely.
Every rule MUST carry >=1 denyExamples and >=1 allowExamples; policy.test.mjs fails otherwise,
so a rule cannot ship untested and cannot be silently loosened without a red.
There is deliberately NO environment-variable bypass. If a rule must be broken, edit this file
in a PR where the diff is visible, or run the command outside the agent.
MCP adapters (2026-10-15): the rules below carry a `tools` allowlist, so a forbidden command delivered through a tool that
runs commands or writes files but is not Bash/PowerShell/Write/Edit/NotebookEdit was never judged. `mcpAdapters` maps such a
tool call onto Bash (commandFields) or Write (pathFields) so EVERY rule applies and no rule text is duplicated. Only the
NAMED fields are read, never content or any other string field, and the native tools are never adapted. Pinned by
scripts/agent-os/mcpCoverage.test.mjs; documented, with what is still unguarded, in docs/agent-os/README.md.
Optional row fields: cwdField, exceptRules (rule ids a row's calls are not judged by; an unknown id is reported and the
exemption ignored, so the rule applies), clientHint (a client word prefixed to typed text), skipWhenTrue (a strict boolean
true means preview only), expandDirectory (judge the files below a moved directory). Each is explained in the README and
pinned by a canary. A named field may hold a string or a LIST of strings (run_sql_transaction.sql_statements): each
element is judged on its own, in order, until 2,000 elements or 1,000,000 characters in total have been judged.
onlyRules (the ONLY rule ids a row's calls are judged by; the reverse of exceptRules; a malformed list, an unknown id or an id of a rule
that cannot judge the row's tool is reported and ignored, so every rule applies) and rawText (a strict boolean true skips the shell
neutraliser and the read-only-search skip, and replaces & | -, so only a row judged by destructive-sql alone may carry it; a declared but
malformed value on a Bash row is reported and the text is judged both as a shell command and as raw SQL, denied if either denies) are set on the four
SQL text rows: SQL is not a shell command. A row whose onlyRules is exactly [destructive-sql] judges a field whole up to 1,000,000 characters.
destructive-sql (extended 2026-10-15): its DELETE / UPDATE / ALTER TABLE ... DROP / DROP-kind arms are probed by the rule's
denyExamples and allowExamples. docs/agent-audit/CONTROL-CANARY-COVERAGE.md states the denyExamples total and
coverage-doc.test.mjs fails when it drifts: change that number in the same commit as any denyExample.
infra-mutation-tool (2026-10-15, job infra-deny-by-name): the Railway, Neon, Vercel and Prisma MCP tools that delete, redeploy, restart, edit variables,
credentials, domains, DNS or schema carry no command text, so the TOOL NAME is the judged text. The adapter row infra-name has `nameAsText: true`
(judge the tool name instead of an input field; Bash row, onlyRules exactly [infra-mutation-tool], no rawText because rawText would erase the hyphens
of the Railway names). Both patterns match the LAST name segment only, never the server segment: connector UUIDs change when a connector is re-added.
The leaf list is the classification in scripts/agent-os/mcpInfraDeny.test.mjs; that file pins both patterns to it. Reads, logs and additive creates
are not in the list. Registered in .claude/settings.json by the pretool-only MCP matcher. Documented in docs/agent-os/README.md > Infra tools: deny by name.

infraApprovals.$comment: Per-action approval of ONE infra-mutation-tool call (job 2026-10-20-infra-approve-per-action, scripts/agent-os/infra-approve.mjs). neverApprovable: leaves no approval lifts (the six outage-class tools, plus every project-level leaf: its input names only a project id, a scope id no approval can name; Codex P2 on PR 3193); a malformed list makes NOTHING approvable. aliases: an approval target -> the ids it also matches as a whole input value; a malformed map adds nothing. The 30-minute window is a constant in code, not here.

mcpAdapters.why: Terminal MCP: types `command` into the operator's interactive PowerShell tab, so every Bash rule applies. `cwd` is where the tab starts, so the cwd-scoped rules judge it as well as the session cwd.

Desktop Commander start_process: runs `command` in a shell on this machine, in Desktop Commander's OWN cwd, not the Claude session cwd. install-in-junctioned-worktree is keyed to the cwd a PROCESS runs in (it protects a worktree's junctioned node_modules), so it is exempt here: the sanctioned global-install path in .claude/skills/harness-worktree-setup/SKILL.md runs through this tool from a worktree session. shared-deps-mutation is exempt for the same reason (2026-10-17): the scratchpad-clone recipe in that SKILL.md section 3 installs a new dependency in an isolated clone through this tool; the residual (this tool pointed at the primary checkout) is documented in docs/agent-os/README.md. Every other rule, the session-scoped night-shift rules included, still judges the call. It is registered twice (plugin name and connector UUID) and the middle segment is not stable, so the tool-name suffix is matched.

Desktop Commander interact_with_process: `input` is text typed into a running shell or REPL. A psql REPL started by an earlier start_process call receives bare SQL, so the typed text is judged as if sent to a SQL client (clientHint is prefixed), except a single read-only search such as grep, which stays a search. Same exemption as start_process (exceptRules).
Native Monitor tool: runs `command` in a background shell. Its {ws} form carries no command and is not judged.

File writers: Desktop Commander write_file, edit_block and write_pdf, and the filesystem MCP server's write_file (docs/codebase-memory-mcp.md). Judged as Write by PATH only: content, old_string and new_string are never scanned.

The filesystem MCP server's edit_file. It takes dryRun: true to preview a diff and write nothing, so only the strict boolean true skips judging. The skip lives on this row alone: no other file tool documents dryRun, and a server that ignores an unknown dryRun would write anyway.

move_file writes the destination and removes the source, so both are judged as Write paths. A DIRECTORY move writes every file below it, so expandDirectory also judges destination/<relative path> for each descendant file (names only, bounded, symlinks never followed, any filesystem error fails open).

Neon run_sql and explain_sql_statement: `sql` is bare SQL, judged as text sent to a psql client (clientHint), so destructive-sql applies. explain_sql_statement with analyze:true EXECUTES the statement, so it is judged exactly like run_sql. Accepted: a hinted row cannot tell a mention from an execution, so a string literal that holds DROP TABLE is denied too. onlyRules limits it to destructive-sql, so a shell rule never denies SQL that merely mentions a command (an INSERT of the words git push origin main) and a rule added later does not silently apply to SQL text; rawText skips the shell neutraliser (it erases the quoted argument after -m/-t/-b, which in SQL can hold statements) and the read-only-search skip. Judged whole up to 1,000,000 characters.

Neon run_sql_transaction: `sql_statements` is a LIST of statements. Each element is judged on its own as text sent to a psql client (clientHint) and is never joined with its neighbours; elements are judged in order until 2,000 of them or 1,000,000 characters in total have been judged, then one stderr line says the rest were not. onlyRules limits it to destructive-sql, so a shell rule never denies SQL that merely mentions a command (an INSERT of the words git push origin main) and a rule added later does not silently apply to SQL text; rawText skips the shell neutraliser (it erases the quoted argument after -m/-t/-b, which in SQL can hold statements) and the read-only-search skip. Judged whole up to 1,000,000 characters.

Neon complete_database_migration re-sends `migration_sql` and applies it to the PARENT branch (apply_changes defaults to true), so it is judged as text sent to a psql client. prepare_database_migration runs on a temporary branch only and is deliberately NOT judged, so a migration stays testable. Accepted: an apply_changes false discard that carries destructive SQL is denied too. onlyRules limits it to destructive-sql, so a shell rule never denies SQL that merely mentions a command (an INSERT of the words git push origin main) and a rule added later does not silently apply to SQL text; rawText skips the shell neutraliser (it erases the quoted argument after -m/-t/-b, which in SQL can hold statements) and the read-only-search skip. Judged whole up to 1,000,000 characters.

Prisma Postgres execute_sql_query and execute_prisma_postgres_schema_update: `query` is bare SQL, judged as text sent to a psql client (clientHint). Registered twice (connector UUID and the Prisma-Remote plugin), so the tool-name suffix is matched. Prisma has its own sponsor approval flow (approvalId); this row is the repo-side text check. onlyRules limits it to destructive-sql, so a shell rule never denies SQL that merely mentions a command (an INSERT of the words git push origin main) and a rule added later does not silently apply to SQL text; rawText skips the shell neutraliser (it erases the quoted argument after -m/-t/-b, which in SQL can hold statements) and the read-only-search skip. Judged whole up to 1,000,000 characters.

Railway, Neon, Vercel and Prisma infra tools: deletes, redeploys, restarts, variable, credential, domain, DNS and schema changes. They carry no command text, so the judged text is the TOOL NAME (nameAsText), judged by infra-mutation-tool alone (onlyRules). rawText is NOT set: it would replace the hyphens the Railway names are made of. The row matches the LAST name segment only, so a connector UUID that changes on reconnect, a plugin name or a claude_ai_ name changes nothing. The leaf list is the classification pinned by scripts/agent-os/mcpInfraDeny.test.mjs. complete_database_migration and execute_prisma_postgres_schema_update are also claimed by their SQL text rows: both rows judge the call, so a destructive statement is attributed to destructive-sql (that row is judged first) and a benign one to the name rule. Nothing lifts the name rule: there is no override and no environment variable.

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: NEVER push or commit directly to main. Named branch + PR, always.
rules.fix: git push -u origin <type>/<task>, then: gh pr create --head <branch> ; gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch
denyExamples: git fetch origin ; git push origin main
allowExamples: git commit -m "docs: forbid git push origin main"

git push origin chore/x 2>&1 | tail -3
gh pr create --head chore/x --base main
git push -u origin chore/x && gh pr create --head chore/x --base main
git push origin docs/y ; gh pr merge 42 --squash --delete-branch

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: never force-push shared history (any form: --force, --force-with-lease, bundled -uf, or a +refspec). Sibling sessions push to these branches. The scan stops at ;/|/& (same technique as push-to-main) so the bundled-short-flag and +refspec arms cannot reach into an unrelated chained command — witnessed 2026-09-01: `git push origin <branch> && gh api ... -f body="..."` was denied because `gh api`'s -f (field) flag matched the bundled-flag arm across the chain boundary.
rules.fix: Rebase and push normally. If a rider commit is in the way, disclose it in the PR body — never rewrite it away.
allowExamples: git push origin statenour/fix-thing && gh api graphql -f query='mutation' -f body="path matches [^/]+\.(ts|tsx)$"

rules.why: Red-team 2026-08-04: `git push`, `git push origin`, and `git push origin HEAD` resolve the destination from the CURRENT branch — which may be main. The push-to-main rule blocks a spelling; this rule blocks the destination being left implicit at all. Red-team 2026-10-01: the first two arms were anchored to the end of the whole command, so an implicit push followed by ;, &&, a pipe, a redirect or a newline passed (15 bypasses through the real hook), while the HEAD arm read past those into later commands and blocked explicit pushes (5 false positives). Every arm now ends at its own command.
rules.fix: Name the full destination explicitly: git push -u origin <branch>  (or  git push origin HEAD:<branch>).
denyExamples:
git add a.ts
git commit -m x
git push
echo done
git push origin HEAD; echo done
allowExamples: git push -u origin feature/x 2>&1 | tail -4; git rev-parse HEAD
git push -u origin feature/x && git log -1 HEAD
git push origin feature/x && echo @ done
git push origin HEAD:feature/x; git rev-parse HEAD

git push origin feature/x
git log -1 HEAD

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: stage only your files by explicit path. Concurrent sessions share this tree; -A/--all/. cross-contaminates apps and sweeps in sibling-session files. 2026-10-25: the scan stops at ; | & and newline (as force-push did 2026-09), so a one-path add chained with a later --root . or ls -A passes, and a dot followed by ; & | ) or written as ".", './' or .\ is caught. Also denied (manager ruling 2026-10-25, each a whole-tree add with no named path): a bare -u/--update, :/ and :(top), a token that starts with * (bare *, './*', '*.ts'), .. and ../, and git's own file list as the path list ($(git ls-files|diff|status ...), backticks, or piped into xargs git add). Still allowed: -u with named paths, apps/x/*.ts, ./docs/a.md, :/apps/x.md, ../app/a.ts.
rules.fix: git add path/to/one.ts path/to/two.ts
denyExamples: pnpm test && git add -A && git commit -m x
allowExamples: git add docs/agent-os/README.md && git commit -m "x -A y"

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: never --no-verify. The lefthook pre-commit/pre-push gate is the last check before shared history. Extended 2026-11-01 (job double-check-missed) to every spelling of switching the hooks off, after FACT 2026-10-30 ~07:40Z: a commit with git's -c option pointing core.hooksPath at a null location passed this rule, whose only pattern was the literal long flag. Covered now: git's unambiguous abbreviations of the flag (git 2.55 accepts --no-veri for commit, --no-v for am); -n, which is --no-verify for git commit and git am only, bundled too (-nm, -anm, -vn); git -c / --config-env core.hooksPath (any verb, any value); GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n> or GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS naming core.hooksPath; a git config write of core.hooksPath (local, worktree, global, system, file, set subcommand); LEFTHOOK, LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE, LEFTHOOK_CONFIG or LEFTHOOK_BIN set before a git verb that runs hooks (the installed .git/hooks scripts exit 0 on LEFTHOOK=0 and run LEFTHOOK_BIN); setx / SetEnvironmentVariable of those. Config keys and env names match in any case. Stays allowed: git push -n (dry run), -n of merge/rebase (no stat) and cherry-pick (no commit), git config reads and --unset (hooks return to .git/hooks, where lefthook installs), LEFTHOOK_VERBOSE/OUTPUT, and mentions: the new arms start at a command position (line start, after ; & | ( or a shell -c), read one command up to ; | & or a newline, and treat a quoted string as one token. Not covered: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM pointing at a crafted file, a git alias defined elsewhere, .git/config edited by a file tool, git called by a full path.
rules.fix: Fix what the hook is complaining about; if the check itself is wrong, change the check in a PR. git push -n (dry run) and git config --get core.hooksPath stay allowed.
denyExamples: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/dev/null git commit -m x
export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'user.name=x' 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null'" && git push origin chore/x
export LEFTHOOK=0; git push origin chore/x
allowExamples: git commit -m "docs: ban git -c core.hooksPath and LEFTHOOK=0"
git commit -m x && git push -n origin chore/x

rules.why: Memory git-sync-never-reset-hard: a sibling session's uncommitted work can be sitting in this tree, and none of these leave a reflog entry for unstaged changes. Covers reset --hard, checkout -- <path>, git clean -d/-f/-x, and worktree-writing git restore. Red-team 2026-10-01: git's other spellings of the same discard passed: checkout . (all paths), checkout <ref> -- <path> and checkout <ref> . (the ref's copy over your edits), checkout -f / --force and switch -f / --force / --discard-changes (switching that throws local changes away). They are covered now, and so is checkout [<ref>] <file> when the word ends in a source-file extension; a bare checkout <word> without one stays allowed, because by text alone it is a branch switch. 2026-10-25: the --staged / --worktree lookaheads stop at ; | & and newline; before that, git restore <file> && git diff --staged was ALLOWED (the --staged of the later command exempted the restore).
rules.fix: Sync with: git fetch origin main ; git merge --ff-only origin/main. A file that reads dirty for line endings only (a CRLF blob under eol=lf) and blocks that fast-forward: node scripts/agent-os/eol-restore.mjs <path> [--ref origin/main] (it refuses a real edit, keeps a backup, stages the ref's blob), then the fast-forward. To discard YOUR OWN edit, copy the file aside first (cp file file.bak). git restore --staged <file> (unstage only) stays allowed. To take another ref's version of a file you have NOT edited, copy the file aside, then redirect git show <ref>:<path> into it from bash, or through cmd /c on Windows (a Windows PowerShell 5.1 > redirect re-encodes the file as UTF-16); during a merge, git checkout --theirs / --ours <path> stays allowed.
denyExamples: git restore --staged a.ts && git restore b.ts
node scripts/agent-os/eol-restore.mjs a.tsx || git restore a.tsx
node scripts/agent-os/eol-restore.mjs a.tsx; git checkout -- a.tsx
allowExamples: git commit -m "chore: use merge --ff-only, not git reset --hard"
node scripts/agent-os/eol-restore.mjs apps/x/a.tsx --ref origin/main && git merge --ff-only origin/main

rules.why: Memory git-stash-pop-steals-sibling-stash: the stash is shared across worktrees. A no-op 'stash push' still exits 0, so pop/apply/branch can restore ANOTHER session's stash into your tree. The same sharing makes drop and clear destructive: they delete stash entries other sessions may own (red-team 2026-10-01). 2026-10-25 (job no-permission-rules): a session may drop only an entry it tagged, and only through scripts/agent-os/stash-drop-tagged.mjs, which finds it by its full manager-* or session-* tag and checks the dropped SHA; a drop by index stays denied even after a git stash list on the same line, because a sibling's push shifts every index.
rules.fix: Copy the file aside instead (cp file file.bak). To set work aside, tag it: git stash push -u -m session-<task>-<date>; read it back with git stash show -p; drop YOUR tagged entry with node scripts/agent-os/stash-drop-tagged.mjs <tag>.
denyExamples: git stash list | grep manager-eol && git stash drop stash@{3}
git stash list; git stash drop stash@{0} # session-x
node scripts/agent-os/stash-drop-tagged.mjs session-x || git stash drop

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: node_modules in a worktree are NTFS junctions pointing OUT at the primary checkout. A recursive delete walks the links and can strip the shared node_modules every session depends on.
rules.fix: powershell scripts/worktree-teardown.ps1 -targetDir .worktrees/<name>   (unlinks junctions first, verifies targets, then removes)

rules.why: Same junction landmine as worktree-remove, reached through the shell instead of git: rm -r / Remove-Item -Recurse on a worktree directory walks the node_modules junctions into the primary checkout.
rules.fix: powershell scripts/worktree-teardown.ps1 -targetDir <worktree>   — it unlinks the junctions first.
allowExamples: Remove-Item Env:\GITHUB_TOKEN -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; gh pr list --state open
git commit -m "docs: note Remove-Item Env:\GITHUB_TOKEN false-positived in the harness sandbox"

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: statenour migrations are hand-applied; pgvector/tsvector columns are Unsupported(...) to Prisma. --accept-data-loss silently drops them, and prisma migrate reset / db push --force-reset destroy strictly more (red-team 2026-08-04).
rules.fix: Hand-apply the migration and verify with prisma migrate status. Skill: statenour-migration.

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: destructive schema commands need an explicit operator instruction. Memory agent-destructive-script-incident: a 'verification' run deleted 870 rows, a class that only DROP and TRUNCATE covered until 2026-10-15; the rule now also denies a DELETE FROM or an UPDATE ... SET with no WHERE in its statement, ALTER TABLE ... DROP and the listed DROP kinds (docs/agent-os/README.md lists the limits and the kinds that pass). The rule requires a DB client on the same command so that grepping/auditing SQL text stays legal — mention is not execution.
rules.fix: Ask the operator. If this is migration SQL, write it to a migration file (Write is not blocked) rather than executing it from a shell. A write meant for a subset needs a WHERE that names it.
denyExamples: psql -c "WITH d AS (DELETE FROM leads RETURNING *) SELECT count(*) FROM d"
psql -c "DELETE FROM a WHERE x; DELETE FROM b;"
psql -c "BEGIN; UPDATE leads SET a = 1; COMMIT;"
psql -c "INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (a) DO UPDATE SET a = excluded.a; UPDATE t SET b = 1"
psql -c "ALTER TABLE leads DROP COLUMN note"
psql -c "alter table leads drop constraint c"
psql -c "ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS ONLY public.leads DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS note"
psql -c "DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'DROP TABLE x'; END $$"
psql -c "DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'DELETE FROM x'; END $$"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "DELETE FROM leads" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM leads WHERE id > 0"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "UPDATE leads SET status = 'x'" -qc "SELECT 1 WHERE true"
ssh host "ssh db \"psql -c \\\"UPDATE public.\\\\\\\"Task\\\\\\\" SET a = 1\\\"\""
printf 'ALTER TABLE t\nDROP FOREIGN KEY fk;' | mysql app
psql "$U" -c "DELETE FROM leads" && psql "$U" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM leads WHERE id > 0"
psql "$U" -c "UPDATE leads SET status = 'x'" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM leads WHERE id > 0"
psql "$U" -c "DELETE FROM leads" | psql "$U" -c "SELECT 1 WHERE true"
allowExamples: psql -c "DELETE FROM t USING u WHERE t.id = u.id"
psql -c "select 1; delete from leads where id = 2;"
psql -c "DELETE FROM a WHERE x; DELETE FROM b WHERE y;"
psql -c "UPDATE leads SET status = 'x' WHERE id = 1"
psql -c "INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (a) DO UPDATE SET a = excluded.a"
mysql -e "INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE a = VALUES(a)"
psql -c "MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET a = s.a WHEN MATCHED AND s.gone THEN DELETE"
psql -c "SELECT * FROM leads FOR UPDATE OF leads SKIP LOCKED"
psql -c "CREATE TABLE a (b int REFERENCES b(id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL, c int REFERENCES c(id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL)"
mysql -e "CREATE TABLE t (updated_at timestamp DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, p int, FOREIGN KEY (p) REFERENCES q(id) ON DELETE SET NULL)"
psql -c "CREATE TRIGGER t BEFORE UPDATE ON leads FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION f()"
psql -c "GRANT UPDATE ON leads TO app"
psql -c "ALTER TABLE leads ADD COLUMN note text"
git commit -m "docs: psql DELETE FROM leads is denied"
psql -c "UPDATE t SET a = b || c WHERE id = 1"
psql -c "UPDATE t SET name = 'AT&T' WHERE id = 1"
psql -c "UPDATE leads SET status = 'x' WHERE id = 1" -c "SELECT 1"
psql -c "DELETE FROM a WHERE x" && psql -c "DELETE FROM b WHERE y"
psql -c "UPDATE t SET a = a -b WHERE id = 1"
psql -h db -d app -tA -c "UPDATE leads SET a = 1 WHERE id = 2" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1

rules.why: Memory never-pnpm-install-in-a-junctioned-worktree: node_modules here are junctions to the PRIMARY checkout. pnpm offers to WIPE them (prompt defaults to yes), breaking every concurrent session at once.
rules.fix: Worktrees are pre-junctioned: no install needed. New or changed deps go through the scratchpad-clone recipe in .claude/skills/harness-worktree-setup/SKILL.md section 3; then the operator (or a primary-checkout session) runs a full, unfiltered pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in the primary when no sibling session is mid-run. Never a filtered install: that shape pruned the shared store on 2026-10-17.

rules.why: 2026-10-17: a session in the PRIMARY checkout ran `pnpm --filter @statenour/web add ts-fsrs`; pnpm pruned vite from the shared node_modules and every junctioned worktree's nickstire tsc and vitest broke at once. Every worktree points at the primary's node_modules, so a package-changing (add/remove/update/prune/dedupe, `yarn workspace <x> add|remove`, `npm install <pkg>` with a positional package) or FILTERED install there rewrites what all sessions run on. Applies in every cwd (no cwd condition): in a worktree install-in-junctioned-worktree is checked first and keeps its verdicts, and this rule also catches the filter-before-verb shape (`pnpm -F x install`) that rule never matched. Allowed: the full unfiltered `pnpm install [--frozen-lockfile]`, scripts and exec, global (-g) installs, and a command that is only echoed or quoted in a commit message.
rules.fix: New or changed deps: use the scratchpad-clone recipe in .claude/skills/harness-worktree-setup/SKILL.md section 3 (install in an isolated clone, copy the lockfile back). Then a full, unfiltered pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in the primary, run by the operator or a primary-checkout session when no sibling session is mid-run. Check the result with node scripts/agent-os/deps-check.mjs.
denyExamples: grep x f && pnpm add zod
node scripts/agent-os/heavy.mjs run -- pnpm --filter x add y
allowExamples: git commit -m "fix the pnpm add guard"
echo "never run pnpm --filter x add y in the primary"
node scripts/agent-os/heavy.mjs run -- pnpm --filter nicks-tire-auto test

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: .env files hold live credentials. Agents must not author them; .env.example is the tracked contract.
rules.fix: Add the variable to .env.example and to the env validator, then ask the operator to set the real value.

rules.why: scripts/night-shift/README.md: Night Shift NEVER merges — a human merge is the only way anything ships. Until 2026-09-15 that was a sentence in a prompt while the unattended agent held the same gh authority as any session (main is unprotected, and the general instructions teach `gh pr merge`). The cwd is the identity: run.ps1 always works in .worktrees/night-shift-<date>. Also denies the ways around the front door (REST/GraphQL merge, auto-merge, /merges, rulesets, branch protection, secrets, workflow toggles).
rules.fix: Open the PR (gh pr create --head night-shift/<date> --base main ...) and stop. The operator merges — or doesn't.
denyExamples: gh api -X POST repos/o/r/merges -f base=main -f head=night-shift/2026-09-15
allowExamples: gh pr create --head night-shift/2026-09-15 --base main --title "never gh pr merge" --body "docs: the operator merges"

rules.why: A Night Shift run may push ONE thing: its own night-shift/<date> branch. Pushing to any other branch (a sibling's, a docs/ branch, a darwin/ branch) is a way to land a change outside the evaluator-separation check that keys on the branch prefix. Two arms: no night-shift ref named at all, OR any additional slash-shaped refspec that is not night-shift/ (a second refspec smuggled beside the legitimate one). push-to-main and push-implicit-dest still fire first for their own shapes.
rules.fix: git push -u origin night-shift/<date>  (the branch run.ps1 created for this run) — one refspec, nothing else
denyExamples: pnpm test && git push -u origin docs/notes
allowExamples:
git push origin night-shift/2026-09-15 2>&1 | tail -3
gh pr create --head night-shift/2026-09-15 --base main --title x --body y
git commit -m "docs: never git push -u origin main from night shift"

rules.why: config/agent-os/evaluator-paths.json: a candidate branch may change the PRODUCT, never the things that JUDGE it. CI (evaluator-separation.yml) catches this after the push; this rule catches it at the keyboard, and adds the two files that decide whether ANY guard runs at all (.claude/settings.json hooks, lefthook.yml). nightShiftPolicy.test.mjs asserts this pattern covers every path in evaluator-paths.json, so the two lists cannot drift apart silently.
rules.fix: If the right fix is an evaluator change, STOP and write it as a finding in the PR body (scripts/night-shift/PROMPT.md rule 1). A judge change is a normal branch, reviewed on its own.

rules.why: Codex review of #2335 (P1): night-shift-no-judge-edits only sees paths from Write/Edit/NotebookEdit, so a Night Shift run could rewrite any judge through the shell — a redirect, tee, sed -i, cp/mv, Set-Content/Out-File, a git checkout/restore of the file, an inline node -e / python -c, or a curl -o — and one such write to policy.json or the hook config disables every guard before the next command. This arm denies the shell shapes that NAME a judge path (built from the same evaluator-paths.json list, plus .claude/settings.json and lefthook.yml). Residual, stated on purpose: a script file the run authored that writes a judge path without naming it in the command is beyond any command-text hook; evaluator-separation.yml catches that after the push, and night-shift-no-merge holds regardless.
rules.fix: Read judges freely (cat/rg/git diff/git log, or run them: node scripts/agent-os/policy.test.mjs). Never write one from a Night Shift run — if the right fix is an evaluator change, STOP and write it as a finding in the PR body (scripts/night-shift/PROMPT.md rule 1).
allowExamples: pnpm --filter nicks-tire-auto exec vitest run tests/episodes
echo "note: config/agent-os/policy.json is a judge" > docs/NIGHT-SHIFT-NOTES.md
git commit -m "docs: never Set-Content config/agent-os/policy.json from night shift"
gh pr create --head night-shift/2026-09-15 --base main --title "x" --body "finding: scripts/agent-os/policy.mjs needs a rule"

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: deletes, redeploys, restarts, variable and credential edits, domain and DNS changes and schema changes on Railway, Neon, Vercel and Prisma need Nour's explicit instruction for the specific action, every time. These MCP tools carry no command text, so this rule judges the TOOL NAME, by its last segment, whatever server segment it has. Native permissions.ask rules written for the same tools did not prompt in bypassPermissions in the 2026-10-15 live check, so this is a hook denial (exit 2), which was proven live the same day. Reads, logs and additive creates are not denied. Per-action approval (2026-10-20): when Nour types the line APPROVE <tool> <target> in chat, exactly one call of that tool whose identifying id fields (branch_id, serviceId ...; not project, environment, org, workspace or team ids, never free text) ALL name that target passes within 30 minutes (scripts/agent-os/infra-approve.mjs); the tools in infraApprovals.neverApprovable never pass.
rules.fix: Do not retry and do not look for another route to the same effect. Tell Nour the exact action (provider, tool, target id, what it changes). He can approve that one call by typing the line APPROVE <tool> <target> in chat (one call, 30 minutes), or he runs it himself in the provider dashboard or CLI, or changes this rule in a PR where the diff is reviewable. Never write an approval yourself. There is no override and no environment variable that lifts it. Railway reads and logs through Bash (railway run, railway variables, railway logs) and MCP reads are not affected.

rules.why: Nour, 2026-10-16: sibling sessions dispatched lanes from prose briefs with the model unspecified, so lanes ran on the wrong tier and nobody could audit what they were told. A lane dispatch (Agent subagent_type lane-*) is judged as one summary line built by policy.mjs > agentDispatchCall.
rules.fix: A prose prompt (the word brief, no file) and a URL do not count: write the brief to a file from .agents/core/templates/subagent-brief.md (v3), name that file path (ending brief.md) in the prompt with its MODEL / EFFORT line, and set the Agent tool's model (and effort) from that line, per the template's routing table.

rules.why: Nour, 2026-10-22: a scout session reported '0 declines ever captured' because its brief carried none of the shop's data meanings (an estimate with no invoice IS the decline). A fresh agent or session does not load the manager's memory, so a brief that reads Nick's Tire records must carry them. Judged on the summary line policy.mjs > agentDispatchCall builds for Agent, Task and mcp__ccd_session__start_session.
rules.fix: Add a line that STARTS with 'SHOP DATA:' (at the start of its own line, not mid-paragraph; it counts in the prompt, start_session background, or the brief file) and paste after it the 'Shop data meanings' lines from .agents/core/USER.md (memory shop-data-meanings): a counter invoice is a closed job and its payment status means nothing (separate register); an estimate with no matching invoice most likely means the customer walked (declined work) but stays an inference; key follow-ups to invoices, not bookings.
denyExamples: lane-dispatch type=lane-nickstire-server model=sonnet brief=C:/x/retention-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=no
session-start model=claude-sonnet-5-5 effort=high brief=C:/x/retention-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=no
allowExamples: lane-dispatch type=lane-nickstire-server model=sonnet brief=C:/x/retention-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=yes
lane-dispatch type=lane-statenour model=sonnet brief=C:/x/ui-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
session-start model=claude-sonnet-5-5 effort=high brief=C:/x/retention-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=yes
session-start model=claude-opus-5-5 effort=high brief=C:/x/hook-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a

rules.why: Nour, 2026-10-25: 'WHY EVERY SESSION STARTING IN FABLE?'. mcp__ccd_session__start_session inherits the parent's model and effort when they are omitted; the manager omitted them on four sessions in a row after a /model switch, so all four ran on the wrong tier. The lane rule (lane-dispatch-brief) covered Agent lanes only. Judged on the session-start summary line policy.mjs > agentDispatchCall builds; a proposal_id-only start and a title-only offer carry no brief and are not judged (the brief was judged when proposed, or is judged when sent with proposal_id).
rules.fix: Pass `model` (opus for design or judgement, sonnet for a known pattern with tests, sonnet or haiku for mechanical work) and `effort` on the start_session call; name the brief FILE (a path ending brief.md, from .agents/core/templates/subagent-brief.md) in `prompt` or `background`; put a 'MODEL / EFFORT: <model> / <effort>' line in the prompt, and a line STARTING 'SHOP DATA:' when the work reads shop records. A fork runs on your own model whatever you pass: when the tier should differ, start it with context fresh.
denyExamples: session-start model=- effort=- brief=no model-effort-line=no shop-data=n/a
session-start model=- effort=high brief=C:/x/hook-fix-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
session-start model=claude-sonnet-5-5 effort=- brief=C:/x/hook-fix-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
session-start model=claude-sonnet-5-5 effort=high brief=no model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
session-start model=claude-opus-5-5 effort=high brief=C:/x/hook-fix-brief.md model-effort-line=no shop-data=yes
allowExamples: session-start model=claude-sonnet-5-5 effort=high brief=C:/x/hook-fix-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
session-start model=claude-opus-5-5 effort=xhigh brief=./briefs/admin-brief.v3.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=yes
session-start model=claude-haiku-5-5 effort=medium brief=C:/x/effort=-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a
lane-dispatch type=lane-platform model=opus brief=C:/x/a-brief.md model-effort-line=yes shop-data=n/a

rules.why: The per-action infra approvals (%LOCALAPPDATA%/nourcity/approvals, job 2026-10-20-infra-approve-per-action) are written ONLY by the UserPromptSubmit hook scripts/agent-os/infra-approve.mjs from Nour's own prompt. A record or a .used marker written, edited or deleted by an agent would create or revive an approval. Any spelling of a nourcity segment followed by an approvals segment is denied: either slash, any case, 8.3 short names, trailing dots, ./ and ../ segments.
rules.fix: Do not touch the approvals store. Ask Nour to type APPROVE <tool> <target> in chat; read the store with the Read tool if you need to see it.

rules.why: The shell door to the same store: a command that names both a nourcity and an approvals path piece (in any order, quoting, variable or separator form, so Join-Path and string pieces are caught), or that runs the writer scripts/agent-os/infra-approve.mjs with node (fed forged stdin it would record an approval), could create or revive an approval. Only the UserPromptSubmit hook may run the writer. A single read-only command (cat, rg ...) is mention, not execution, and passes; a pieced-together name built to dodge the match is not caught (the README says so).
rules.fix: Do not write, delete or move anything in the approvals store and do not run infra-approve.mjs. Ask Nour to type APPROVE <tool> <target> in chat. To test the writer, run node --test scripts/agent-os/infraApprove.test.mjs.
